sourcePolicy.name: Manual exact-NORAD official-source review
sourcePolicy.identityRule: Index by canonical NORAD catalog ID, then require the current object name, international designator, and exact SATCAT type to match the reviewed record.
sourcePolicy.purposeRule: Use only purpose text supported by the cited authoritative mission source; never infer object-specific purpose from name, type, owner, group, or orbit. Separately labeled constellation context describes the service, not an individual object's purpose or operational status.
sourcePolicy.imageRule: Bundle only an image reviewed as depicting the exact object, with explicit public-display and transformation rights.
sourcePolicy.takedownProcedure: Remove the manifest record and bundled asset, run npm run check:orbital-enrichment, and deploy the resulting exact source revision. Never substitute a generic object image.

starlink.description: Starlink describes its service as internet access at home and on the go, including rural and remote locations.

purpose.description: NASA describes Hubble as a large space-based observatory used to observe the universe and expand understanding of the cosmos.
purpose.identityEvidence: The reviewed CelesTrak visual snapshot identifies NORAD 20580 as HST, international designator 1990-037B, type PAY. The NASA page explicitly identifies the Hubble Space Telescope and its observatory purpose.

purpose.description: Terra was designed to study interactions among Earth's atmosphere, land, oceans and radiant energy. Its measurements support research into environmental change and natural hazards, including fires and volcanoes.
purpose.identityEvidence: The reviewed CelesTrak visual catalog identifies NORAD 25994 as TERRA, 1999-068A, PAY. NASA's Terra mission page identifies the same Earth Observing System spacecraft and describes its mission.

purpose.description: Aqua was designed to measure Earth's water cycle, including atmospheric water vapor, clouds, precipitation, snow and ice. Its instruments also investigate temperatures, vegetation, ocean biology and Earth's energy balance.
purpose.identityEvidence: The reviewed CelesTrak visual catalog identifies NORAD 27424 as AQUA, 2002-022A, PAY. NASA identifies Aqua as its Earth Observing System spacecraft launched on 2002-05-04 and describes the water-cycle mission.

purpose.description: Midori II (ADEOS-II) was built to investigate global environmental change. Its microwave and optical sensors were designed to measure water-related conditions, oceans, land, clouds and the atmosphere.
purpose.sourceTitle: Advanced Earth Observing Satellite-II Midori II
purpose.identityEvidence: The reviewed CelesTrak visual catalog identifies NORAD 27597 as MIDORI II (ADEOS-II), 2002-056A, PAY. JAXA explicitly equates Midori II with ADEOS-II and dates its launch to 2002-12-14.

purpose.shortLabel: Radar observation of land and disasters
purpose.description: ALOS-2 (Daichi-2) carries L-band synthetic-aperture radar designed for day-and-night, all-weather observation. Its mission includes disaster mapping, land and infrastructure information, agriculture and tropical-forest monitoring.
purpose.identityEvidence: The reviewed CelesTrak visual catalog identifies NORAD 39766 as ALOS-2, 2014-029A, PAY. JAXA explicitly identifies Daichi-2 as ALOS-2 and documents its radar payload and mission objectives.

purpose.description: Hitomi (ASTRO-H) was designed to study galaxy clusters, black holes and matter under extreme conditions using X-ray and gamma-ray instruments. NASA records that contact was lost in March 2016 and recovery efforts ended in April 2016; this is its historical mission, not a claim of current operation.
purpose.identityEvidence: The reviewed CelesTrak visual catalog identifies NORAD 41337 as ASTRO-H (HITOMI), 2016-012A, PAY. NASA explicitly states that ASTRO-H was renamed Hitomi after its 2016-02-17 launch.

purpose.description: XRISM is a JAXA/NASA mission with ESA participation, designed to investigate celestial X-ray sources. Its Resolve spectrometer and Xtend imager measure X-ray energies and images to study hot, energetic matter in the universe.
purpose.identityEvidence: The reviewed CelesTrak visual catalog identifies NORAD 57800 as XRISM, 2023-137A, PAY. NASA names the same mission, its instruments and its 2023-09-07 Japan-time launch.

purpose.description: NASA's Advanced Composite Solar Sail System demonstrates lightweight, deployable composite booms that support a solar sail. The technology is intended to enable larger sails for propulsion using sunlight.
purpose.identityEvidence: The reviewed CelesTrak visual catalog identifies NORAD 59588 as ACS3, 2024-077B, PAY. NASA's ACS3 mission page expands the mission name and documents the composite-boom solar-sail demonstration.
